prompt:
Research what the Rust project officially documents about its release cadence and how long each stable version is supported. Cite the official Rust page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Rust project operates on a rapid release cycle, issuing new stable versions every six weeks. Regarding support duration, Rust does not offer long-term support (LTS) versions in the traditional sense; instead, only the most recent stable version is officially supported for production use, although older toolchains remain available for download.

SOURCE: https://forge.rust-lang.org/release/process.html | QUOTE: "Rust has a 6 week release cycle." | CLAIM: The official release cadence for Rust is every six weeks.

SOURCE: https://www.rust-lang.org/policies/support | QUOTE: "Only the current stable release is officially supported." | CLAIM: Each stable version is supported only until the next stable version is released, meaning there is no extended support period for previous versions.
